title: As faith grows or weakens, so the sense of God’s favor and our standing in grace strengthens or fades
source_text: XXX. Caeterum, prout fides, vel major, vel minor est; vividior sive languidior: ita quoque sui sensum majorem, vel minorem, acriorem, vel remissiorem animis nostris ingignit. Unde est quod crescente & augescente fide, fiducia illa de Dei erga nos amore & favore, & nostra apud Deum gratia atque justitia, eadem proportione roboratur atque invalescit; & ex adverso minuitur, atque debilitatur, qua ratione fides decrescit atque remittitur.
pass_a_gloss: For the rest, according as faith is greater or lesser, more vivid or more languid, so also it begets in our minds a greater or lesser, sharper or remisser sense of itself. Hence it is that as faith grows and increases, that confidence concerning God’s love and favor toward us and our grace and righteousness before God is strengthened and grows strong in the same proportion; and on the contrary it is diminished and weakened in the measure in which faith decreases and is remitted.
pass_b_english: Assurance tracks faith’s vigor: as faith grows, confidence of divine favor strengthens; as faith flags, assurance softens.
